name: TextArea
purpose: Let a user write or edit multi-line free text - notes, descriptions, comments - in a bordered, resizable field.
intent: The multi-line counterpart of Text Field: a real native <textarea> in the same bordered frame, sharing Text Field's size, context, invalid, and state treatment so the two read as one family. Grouped with Text Field as a molecule for that reason, though it composes no other component.

figmaSource.note: Filed on the file's own "🚧 Text Area" page, verified directly against the file via the Desktop Bridge plugin. The `sm` size was removed on 2026-08-27 (it read almost identically to md); the size axis is now md/lg. variantCount reflects that removal (was 96), re-confirmed live as 64 on 2026-10-13.
figmaSource.structure: One component set across six axes - `type` (default / rich-inline), `size` (md / lg), `context` (default / inline), `state` (default / hover / focus / typing / filled / autofill), `isDisabled`, `isInvalid`. Each variant is a single `Container` frame holding the text; the visual frame (fill, border, radius) is bound on the component node, not the inner Container (which carries only padding). Geometry measured per size: padding block/inline md 8/8, lg 12/12; radius lg (8) at md, xl (12) at lg; font body-md (14/24) at md, body-lg (16/24) at lg. State frame tokens (context=default): default fill background/input/default + border/input 1px; hover fill background/input/hovered; focus fill background/input/pressed + border/focused 2px; typing border/focused 2px; filled = default; autofill layers color/background/autofill/default (16% opacity since 2026-10-14, was 8%) over the default fill and keeps the border/input 1px stroke (re-checked 2026-10-13), which code applies when the textarea is autofilled; invalid border/error 2px; disabled background/disabled + border/disabled. context=inline has a transparent box; hover adds the hover fill and a bottom-only accent (border/input), and focus (border/focused) / invalid (border/error) reveal a bottom-only line, bottom corners square; autofill has no fill or stroke, the same as filled (its two fills, elevation/surface/raised/default + background/autofill/default, were removed on 2026-10-14, per design feedback).
apiAdaptationNotes: Refactored from a bare <textarea> to a wrapper <div> pattern (matching Text Field) to support a trailing icon/action slot (iconAfter). The wrapper div gets the frame styling (border, background, radius, padding) and uses display: flex; align-items: flex-start to lay out the textarea and the optional action slot side by side. The textarea is a transparent, borderless child inside the wrapper, with flex: 1 1 auto. Focus detection uses :focus-within on the wrapper instead of :focus on the textarea. The browser's native resize grip still works: resize: inherit on the textarea, with overflow: auto on the wrapper's resize_* classes (CSS requires overflow != visible for resize to work on a div).

Added an iconAfter slot (React.ReactNode) for a trailing icon or interactive control (e.g. an edit pencil IconButton). Rendered in a span.action wrapper, flex: 0 0 auto. Not aria-hidden - it may hold a real focusable action. context=inline combined with iconAfter is the standard pattern for embedding inside a Key Value Pair.

context=inline (Figma's context=inline) is for a field inside a row, such as Key Value Pair wrapped in Inline Edit. Transparent at rest (no border or background). Hover shows the raised-surface hover background + a bottom accent (border/input), focus shows a bottom-only 2px focus border (border-bottom-color + bottom-only box-shadow), invalid shows a bottom-only error border the same way, and disabled stays transparent. Top corners keep the size's radius; bottom corners are square. The field keeps its normal padding and height so it reads as a real input when activated.

Figma's `context` axis (default/inline) is the `context` prop - the same name and values its sibling Text Field uses, so the two components share one vocabulary. It replaces the earlier `appearance` prop (default/subtle/inline), which is deprecated but still accepted: subtle and inline both map to context=inline, default to context=default. The old code-only appearance=inline look (subtle without the hover background) was merged into context=inline.

Figma binds a newer `background/input/*` + `border/focused` token naming that has no counterpart in this build. Those map one-to-one onto the `elevation/surface/raised/*` + `border/focus` semantic tokens Text Field already consumes (same intent), so Text Area reuses those rather than inventing unbacked tokens - keeping it visually identical to Text Field per token governance's reuse-first rule.

Focus and invalid replace the border color and paint the extra pixel via an inset box-shadow rather than a real 1px->2px border-width change - the same technique Text Field uses, so the multi-line text never shifts by a pixel on focus/blur or invalid toggle.

Figma tints the fill on focus (`background/input/pressed`); code deliberately keeps the resting fill on focus instead, matching Text Field's established no-tint-on-focus behavior (and that token does not exist here).

The `state` axis (hover/focus/typing/filled/autofill) is not a prop - those are live pseudo-classes (`:hover`, `:focus`, `:autofill`), with a documentation-only `data-force-state` pin mirroring hover/focus/autofill for static Storybook reference, exactly as Text Field, Button, and Checkbox do. `filled` and `typing` need no distinct styling (they render as default/focus).

Autofill gets the same treatment as Text Field: when the textarea matches :autofill, or under the data-force-state='autofill' pin, except when disabled, the frame's background layers --color-background-autofill-default over --color-elevation-surface-raised-default, keeping each context's resting stroke. Per explicit design feedback (2026-10-14), hover replaces the tint (the hover rules outrank the autofill rule and set the background shorthand), focus and invalid keep it, and context=inline stays chromeless at rest, as Figma's inline autofill variant does, showing the tint only while focused, which Figma doesn't draw. The browser's own !important autofill fill on the textarea is hidden with background-clip: text, with -webkit-text-fill-color/caret-color replacing its forced text color. No transition: the long-transition workaround needs a raw timing the motion rules don't allow.

The `type=rich-inline` variant is implemented as a separate component, `RichTextArea` (molecules/text-area/rich). It is an inline entity-tagging mode - visually identical to `default`, the difference is entirely behavioral: `/` opens a grouped entity picker and each choice is inserted inline as a navigational tag. It is separate rather than a `type` prop because its value (a structured node array), its callbacks (`onSearch`), and its surface (contenteditable) are all disjoint from the plain <textarea>. TextArea therefore still exposes no `type` prop; reach for RichTextArea instead.

Adds a `resize` prop (none/vertical/horizontal/both, default vertical) mapping to the CSS `resize` property - not a Figma axis, but the standard, expected control for a text area. A disabled field locks resize to none.

size.description: Padding, radius, and font size. body-md at sm/md, body-lg at lg. Auto-resize starts at the matching TextField control height.

context.description: default = bordered box (all corners rounded). inline = chromeless at rest; raised-hover background and a bottom-only border on hover, bottom-only focus/error line on focus/invalid; keeps padding and top-corner radius, square bottom corners — for a field inside a row, such as Key Value Pair wrapped in Inline Edit. Same name and values as Text Field's and Figma's `context`.

appearance.description: Deprecated - use context. subtle and inline map to context='inline', default to 'default'. Still accepted; an explicit context wins.

invalid.description: Sets aria-invalid and paints the error border (via box-shadow, no layout shift).

resize.description: Which edges the user can drag. Maps to CSS `resize`. Disabled fields lock to none.

autoResize.description: Grow and shrink with content, starting at the matching control-size height. Overrides rows and manual resizing; remeasures on value and width changes.

maxRows.description: Maximum visible lines with autoResize before vertical scrolling.

disabled.description: Native textarea disabled; greys the frame and locks resize.

rows.description: Native attribute controlling initial height; overridden by autoResize.

iconAfter.description: A trailing icon or interactive control (e.g. an edit pencil IconButton) rendered after the textarea. Not aria-hidden - it may hold a real focusable action.

className.description: Composes with the wrapper div's class list.

...rest.description: Every native textarea attribute (value, defaultValue, placeholder, maxLength, onChange, name, required, readOnly, wrap, ...) forwards to the element. A ref forwards to the <textarea>.

default.purpose: The standard bordered box, rounded on all four corners. Correct for nearly every case.

inline.purpose: Chromeless at rest; raised-hover background and a bottom-only border on hover, bottom-only focus/error line on focus/invalid, square bottom corners. Keeps the field's normal padding, height, and top-corner radius so it reads as a real input when activated. For a field inside a row, such as Key Value Pair wrapped in Inline Edit.

accessibility.label: No built-in label - pair with a native <label htmlFor> or aria-label, the same as Text Field and any native form control.
accessibility.invalid: aria-invalid reflects the invalid prop; the error is also conveyed visually by the border.
accessibility.disabled: native disabled - removed from the tab order and non-editable.
accessibility.focus: the wrapper's own focus border is the focus affordance (via :focus-within, since the focusable textarea is a child of the wrapper).
accessibility.iconAfter: iconAfter is never forced aria-hidden - it may hold a real interactive control (e.g. an IconButton) which must keep its own accessible name and stay keyboard-reachable.

tokens.autofill: --color-background-autofill-default layered over --color-elevation-surface-raised-default (context=default unless hovered; context=inline only while focused)
tokens.note: All reused from Text Field (including the existing semantic autofill token) - no new tokens. See apiAdaptationNotes for the Figma `background/input/*` -> `elevation/surface/raised/*` naming mapping.

do: Give the textarea an accessible name (a wired <label htmlFor> or aria-label).
Use Text Area for multi-line free text; use Text Field for a single line.
Set `rows` to a sensible initial height for the expected content.
Keep `resize="vertical"` (the default) unless a fixed layout truly needs `none`.
dont: Don't use Text Area for a single-line value - use Text Field.
Don't use it to choose from a fixed set of options - use Select.
Don't use Text Area when the text needs to link to records - use RichTextArea, its inline entity-tagging sibling.
behaviorNotes: The frame styling lives on a wrapper <div>, matching Text Field's pattern. The <textarea> is a transparent, borderless child inside it.
Focus detection uses :focus-within on the wrapper (not :focus on the textarea directly).
Focus/invalid paint the thicker border via inset box-shadow on the wrapper, so the text never shifts.
Hover tint is suppressed once the field is focused.

An autofilled field (the textarea matches :autofill) layers --color-background-autofill-default over the raised surface and keeps each context's resting stroke. Hover replaces the tint; focus and invalid keep it; context=inline stays chromeless at rest and shows the tint only while focused. The browser's own autofill fill on the textarea is hidden.
A disabled field cannot be resized.
iconAfter renders a trailing icon or interactive control at the end of the wrapper row.

context='inline' is chromeless at rest, with the raised-hover background and a bottom-only border on hover and a bottom-only focus/error line on focus/invalid — keeps padding, height, and top-corner radius.
The deprecated appearance prop maps to context: subtle and inline map to inline, default to default. An explicit context wins.
knownLimitations: No built-in label, helper text, or character-count chrome - wrap it in Field for the label, helper text, and error message.
